clinicalPearls: Caused by biallelic mutations in IL7R encoding the alpha chain of the interleukin-7 receptor, which pairs with the common gamma chain to drive thymic T-cell development.
Distinctive immunophenotype is T-B+NK+: T cells are profoundly absent while both B cells and natural killer cells are preserved.
The preserved NK compartment separates it from X-linked and JAK3 SCID (T-B+NK-), because NK development depends on interleukin-15 rather than interleukin-7.
Autosomal recessive inheritance affects both sexes; it is one of the more frequent causes of SCID identified through newborn screening.
B cells are present but functionally inadequate without T-cell help, so antibody responses are poor despite normal B-cell numbers.
Presents in early infancy with failure to thrive, chronic diarrhoea, persistent candidiasis and opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis pneumonia.
Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is curative and most successful when undertaken early; the disorder is not radiosensitive.
Live vaccines and non-irradiated cellular blood products must be avoided to prevent disseminated infection and transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease.
reference.pathophysiology: The interleukin-7 receptor is a heterodimer of the IL-7 receptor alpha chain (encoded by IL7R) and the common gamma chain. Signalling through this receptor via the JAK-STAT pathway delivers the survival and proliferation cues that developing thymocytes require to progress through T-cell maturation. Loss of the alpha chain abolishes interleukin-7 signalling specifically, arresting T-cell development and producing profound T lymphopenia. Because the common gamma chain and the interleukin-15 pathway that governs natural killer cell development remain intact, NK cells are generated normally; B-cell development, which in humans does not depend on interleukin-7 signalling to the same degree, is also preserved. The result is the T-B+NK+ immunophenotype. Although B cells are present, the absence of functional T-cell help leaves humoral immunity ineffective, so the infant suffers the full combined immunodeficiency susceptibility to viral, fungal, bacterial and opportunistic pathogens once maternal antibody declines.
additionalDifferentials: X-linked (IL2RG) and JAK3 SCID, distinguished by absent NK cells (T-B+NK-)
CD3 chain or CD45 deficiency causing T-cell-negative combined immunodeficiency
Coronin-1A deficiency with impaired thymic egress
RAG or Artemis deficiency, excluded by the presence of B cells
Secondary lymphopenia from severe congenital infection
additionalInvestigations: Lymphocyte subset flow cytometry demonstrating the T-B+NK+ pattern
Serum immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses interpreted against maternal IgG
T-cell proliferation assays to mitogens showing absent responses
T-cell receptor repertoire analysis revealing markedly restricted diversity
IL7R gene sequencing to confirm the causative mutation
Evaluation for maternal T-cell engraftment as a confounder
HLA typing of patient and family to plan transplantation
redFlags: Opportunistic infection such as Pneumocystis pneumonia in an infant
Failure to thrive with persistent thrush and chronic diarrhoea
Absent thymic shadow on chest imaging
Erythroderma or hepatosplenomegaly suggesting engraftment or transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease
Severe isolated T lymphopenia with preserved B and NK cells on screening
reference.prognosis: Without immune reconstitution the disorder is fatal in early childhood from infection. Early haematopoietic stem cell transplantation yields high survival and good T-cell recovery, and the preserved NK and B compartments can favour engraftment outcomes.
pitfalls: Normal total lymphocyte or B-cell counts can mask the profound T-cell defect if naive T cells are not specifically assessed.
Maternal IgG may normalise measured immunoglobulins in early infancy despite absent functional antibody.
The preserved NK compartment may be mistaken for reassuring immune competence.
Live vaccines and non-irradiated blood products are hazardous once SCID is suspected.
Maternal engraftment can generate circulating T cells that confound subset interpretation.
references: International primary immunodeficiency classification and management guidelines
National newborn screening and SCID management guidance
management: Arrange urgent allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the only curative treatment, ideally before infection supervenes
Institute protective isolation, avoid all live vaccines, and use only irradiated, CMV-negative, leucodepleted blood products
Give antimicrobial prophylaxis including co-trimoxazole against Pneumocystis, together with antifungal and antiviral cover
Provide immunoglobulin replacement to compensate for absent T-cell help and poor antibody responses despite preserved B cells
Treat active opportunistic infections aggressively and support failure to thrive with nutritional care
Offer genetic counselling and cascade family screening for this autosomal recessive disorder, flagged through newborn screening
